findings.title: Names without warrant
findings.claim: The names assigned by the worshipers and their fathers do not constitute an authorized object of worship; the focus relocates authority to divine judgment, commanded worship, and upright order.
findings.mechanism: The focus naming terms contact proof, judgment, worship, din, and qayyim, while the immediate 12:39 contrast supplies scattered lords versus the one overpowering Lord. The named label is therefore tested by warrant and by the ordered practice that follows.
findings.reader_payoff: Naming becomes an accountable relay: a designation can identify, but it cannot create a lord, a judgment, or a way of life without proof and command.
findings.containment: This preserves ordinary naming while denying that inherited designation itself supplies divine authority. It does not claim that every name is false or that human language is illegitimate.

epistemic.reason: The channel is trusted and its five support items converge on exact focus carriers, the immediate 12:39 contrast, and the focus proof/judgment/worship sequence.

findings.title: d_name_as_relay

findings.title: o_custom_paves_servitude
findings.claim: Inherited practice can pave its own road into servitude; the upright din is warranted and sustaining, not merely familiar.
findings.mechanism: The supplied focus anchor links inherited naming, worship, din, and qayyim to the repeated-practice context: the road image models how custom can become easier to follow and redirect service into servitude.
findings.reader_payoff: Repetition explains how inherited practice can become servitude by smoothing a path, while the upright order is measured by warrant and sustaining effect rather than familiarity.
findings.containment: The changed reading is retained as an attributed pericope hypothesis: before, People consciously choose to serve inherited false gods.; after, Inherited practice can pave its own road into servitude; the upright din is warranted and sustaining, not merely familiar..  The road image is cross-domain but remains anchored in worship, din, qayyim, and nearby persistent practice. It should be presented as a social-mechanism analogy, not as a replacement for ordinary lexical meanings.
